summary: # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video ## Making a Knotted Triangle Scarf (Part 1): Building the Basic Structure In this video, I'm going to show you how to create a square with a diameter of 750mm and a height of 750mm using a 2D window. ### Creating the Square After selecting the rectangular tool, click on the 2D window to create a square with a width of 750mm and a height of 750mm. Since the whole process of making a triangle is in a vertical form, we need to rotate the board first to make it more convenient to use the function of shrinkage. ### Rotating the Board Drag the point on the frame to rotate the board to the position of the picture. The board generated in the software is automatically created when the fabric direction is established. To conveniently use the elastic band shrinkage control fabric, we need to match the direction of the gusset and the board. ### Creating the Folding Line Use the inner line tool to create a folding line. Click on the starting point and double-click on the end point. On the board, right-click to select the 2D arrangement position. You can arrange it to the same position as the 2D window. ### Flipping the Triangle Board Next, let's flip the triangle board. Before we make the gusset, we will keep it in a folding state. Use the folding arrangement tool to select the inner line and drag the corresponding axis to fold the board. Be careful to keep it facing out. ### Fixing the Gusset Select the line of the grid tool group. In the drop-down menu, select the fixed needle tool, and click on the left and right two points to fix them in 3D space. To prevent the gusset from being unstable when rotating, first sew up the side of the same side after folding. Set the sewing line type to "Turned." This will ensure that the sewing line type of "Turned" will automatically flatten and not bulge, affecting the modeling. ### Wrapping the Gusset Turn on the modeling. Drag the fixed needle to wrap the gusset around the virtual model. During this process, you need to change the perspective frequently to prevent the gusset from being misplaced due to visual deviations. ### Simulating Compression Because the board will be compressed significantly in the folding position, we can simulate this compression by reducing the shrinkage. Use the editing logic tool. You will see that the board is in the direction of the gusset, with the arrowhead pointing forward and the vertical axis pointing upward. ### Tying the Knot Now, if we want to tie the knot, it must be compressed along the triangle direction without changing the length of the gusset. Here, we choose to reduce the shrinkage gradually to 60%. Turn on the simulation and adjust the position of the fixed needle during the simulation process. Slowly tighten the gusset and move it down, ensuring the gusset is tightened properly. ### Checking the Gusset Position Next, we will go back to the front and check if the position of the gusset is correct. Due to the shrinkage, we need to leave some space in case it shifts. Fix the creases and ensure that the shape is more suitable and the neckline is not crooked before starting to cut the plate. ### Cutting the Plate It can be troublesome to manually cut in Marvelous Designer. Usually, we will create the cutting effect through the combination of multiple plates. Click near the banana position on the two sides of the scarf to see the corresponding position in the 2D window. Create an inner line near this position to cut the plate. Copy and paste to the corresponding position on the other side. ### Seam Allowance Adjustment If the inner line is not related to the outer line of the plate, select the outer line of the plate from the right-click menu. Choose the two inner lines and cut the seam allowance. You can either cut the seam allowance or leave it as is. Currently, the two sides of the plate are sewn together. To facilitate subsequent modifications, you can delete the seam allowance first and sew the large piece of the plate on the left and right sides together to form a ring that can be put on the neck. ### Activating the Panels Reverse-activate the two small plates cut down. Use Shift + Q to hide the plate. Turn on the simulation and adjust the dress position. The dress position can be modified by 100 to confirm the scarf effect from a formal angle. ### Finalizing the Design After that, fix the two small plates on the back side and sew them together. Otherwise, too many layers and folds will not be stable. If the front panel of the freeze-dry is adjusted, and you have changed the filter, revert it back. Activate the two panels and display them. ### Positioning the Panels Position the two panels correctly. In this video, I placed the panels on one side of the 2D window together. Check the seam side. First, sew up the side of the plate with the fold. Then sew up the side that is close to the hanging part and the side after hanging. Finally, add a knot in the middle, and it will be complete. ### Sewing the Panels Put the inner line together with the outer line of the plate and add points. This way, when using the sewing tool, you can automatically identify the inner line and the side lines. Then sew up the two panels on the top and bottom. Note that the direction of the mark is the opposite, as it is folded. ### Adjusting the Sewing Lines Press the W key to click on the panel in the 3D window. The position of the click will be adjusted. To prevent subsequent instability, change the folded sewing line type to "Turned." Now we need to make three lines. All the sewing lines should be the same. Since we don't have a cut on the panel, we can't sew the line; therefore, we change it to "Turned." ### Creating Free Sewing Lines To determine the length of the line, click the button to create a free sewing line. Then, on the side of the panel, click the button to create another sewing line. On the other side, click to create a sewing line on the opposite side. Click on the blue support point to create a long sewing line. Press W to click on the fixed needle that has been created, and you can delete the fixed needle. ### Preventing Instability Since the two panels are on the same side, there is also a gap. To prevent instability, it is better to change the type of sewing line to "Turned" first. Unscrew the large panel and model it together. The other side will require the same operation. ### Adjusting DNA Similarities What should be the size of the DNA similarities or differences between the three panels? To achieve the best fit, we will change the size of the DNA similarity to match it. To get the best fit, increase the size of the DNA similarity, as there is a maximum scale for it. Additionally, reduce the size of the DNA similarity. ### Optimizing Simulation Settings For a more stable simulation effect, reduce the particle diameter to 15, increase the number of fabric faces, and reduce the conflict thickness to 1. The surface diameter around the virtual model should also be reduced to 1, which will decrease the air distance reserved. ### Final Adjustments After stabilizing, reduce the zoom to 40 to simulate the tightness. Adjust the position of the fixed needle so that the two small plates remain horizontal. Avoid hammering too hard, as this may affect the cutting effect. When using fixed needles to secure a part of the plate, ensure that the plate is not overly stretched. ### Applying Elasticity To make the position tighter, we can apply elasticity to the line section. We applied shrinkage just now. If the ratio of elasticity is higher than that of shrinkage, the elasticity will stretch the line section, which is incorrect. Therefore, we need to set a relatively small ratio. ### Length Adjustment To prevent the impact of force, we need to adjust the length of the line section. The length of the line section behind the edge of the joint is limited. If the width is insufficient, the joint may be pulled out, which is undesirable. To avoid this, adjust the length of the line section. ### Conclusion This concludes the basic production steps for making a knotted triangle scarf in Marvelous Designer. Thank you for watching!
